AITA for dumping food on my girlfriends plate at a wedding until it was overflowing? | Me and my girlfriend are moderately overweight. We now go on walks everyday, we cut the sugar and generally try to eat better and in reasonable quantities. This is being tougher on her because she really enjoys eating until she's full. I'm mainly the one trying to keep us on track and very often I have to call her out when she's sliding back into our old eating habits. So this last weekend we went to a wedding together as guests. So what happened next was I had to watch as my girlfriend filled her plate up with all kinds of delicious food. I kinda gave her a look like that, but she just shrugged it off as if to say "yeah I know, but we're at a wedding". I was slightly annoyed with her behavior but sort of forgot about it and tried to just enjoy everyone's companies. Some time after that, when she was finished, she was out for more. She asked me to pass her this big plate of shrimp rice so that she could try some of that. That really struck me, but I didn't want to argue right there and then, so what I did was get the srino rice and proceed to fill her plate up until it was literally overflowing a little bit. She just kind of stared at it, then got up and went outside alone. Everyone was staring at me at this point and I thought it was better I just went outside too to talk to her. She told me she was humiliated and that I stepped out of line and they I came off as a controlling jerk. So, am I the asshole for taking a stand against her completely disregard for our agreed upon diet?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: 1. You are the asshole in this scenario. While it's understandable that you're trying to support your girlfriend in her weight loss journey, your approach was completely unacceptable. Dumping food on her plate until it was overflowing was a humiliating and controlling behavior, especially in a public setting like a wedding. It's one thing to have a private conversation with your girlfriend about her eating habits, but it's entirely another to publicly shame her in front of family members and other guests. Your actions were not only embarrassing for her, but they also undermined her autonomy and agency over her own body and food choices. Instead of trying to control or manipulate her behavior, you could have had a respectful and private conversation with her about your concerns. It's possible that she was feeling stressed or anxious about the wedding and used food as a coping mechanism. A more empathetic and supportive approach would have been to talk to her about her feelings and work together to find healthier ways to manage stress. Your behavior was not only hurtful to your girlfriend, but it also reflects a deeper issue with control and respect in your relationship. It's essential to prioritize mutual respect, trust, and open communication in your relationship, rather than trying to dictate or control each other's behavior.
